replacements.after: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K\subset S^3$

replacements.before: [F6] [[lem-countable-analytic-choice-for-fixed-sutured-floer-data]] supplies the Countable Choice selection branch for the actual local analytic constructions used in F2–F4 on the fixed finite diagram/cut hierarchy. The pointwise Fredholm parametrices, domain-area bounds, protected-divisor barriers, finite-dimensional Sard reductions and local gluing constructions are those already constructed at these actual targets. Their choices are made on countable separable chart covers as specified in F6; the proof does not invoke the broader full-Choice existence declaration as an assumption. The geometric hierarchy and its finite diagram words are chosen for this one manifold and have only finitely many stages.
replacements.after: [F6] **Classical analytic input and exact axiom boundary.** Under the Axiom of Choice in the Statement, use the general integral sutured analytic framework explicitly imported in E1 of [[lem-integral-sutured-floer-compactness-and-orientations]], at the actual balanced/adapted diagrams, admissibility, boundary-region/divisor and coherent-orientation conditions of F2–F4. This supplies the pointwise Fredholm, regularity, compactification and strip/polygon gluing prerequisite; the preserved local area, grading, signed cut and hierarchy constructions then use it at their stated targets. The published framework is Juhász, *Holomorphic discs and sutured manifolds*, §§3,6–7, especially Definition7.1 and Theorems7.2/7.5, together with the referenced Ozsváth–Szabó analytic framework, and Juhász, *Floer homology and surface decompositions*, Proposition7.6 and Theorems1.4–1.5. These are explicit external inputs in the classical setting, not a newly reconstructed weak-choice theorem. [[lem-countable-analytic-choice-for-fixed-sutured-floer-data]] retains its conditional Countable Choice conclusion: GIVEN the actual pointwise constructions, its fixed finite diagram/cut and at-most-two-parameter choices are finite or countable. It does not itself prove that those pointwise constructions follow under Countable Choice. The Countable-Choice-only genus strengthening is not certified here; neither its falsity nor an independent new geometric open problem is asserted. [Juhász2006](https://msp.org/agt/2006/6-3/agt-v6-n3-p16-s.pdf), [Juhász2008](https://msp.org/gt/2008/12-1/gt-v12-n1-p07-s.pdf)

replacements.before: 2.1 Apply the restricted branch F6 to the fixed finite hierarchy and its diagram choices: the integer domain classes, required finite parameter families, separable Sobolev/perturbation spaces and protected neighborhoods are exactly the inputs described there. This makes the simultaneous regular data, compactness extractions, gluing charts and determinant selections under Countable Choice. With these choices, apply the actual construction F3 to the marked Seifert surface F. Its meridional frame, rather than an unspecified closure framing, gives an admissible adapted representative. By F4 every generator has Alexander degree g−n_P(x), with n_P(x) a nonnegative integer. Hence its whole integral chain complex has no generator, and thus no homology, in a grading greater than g. [F3, F4, F6, step 1.3]
replacements.after: 2.1 Work under the full-Choice analytic framework F6 on the actual fixed finite hierarchy and marked adapted diagram. Its admitted sutured operator problems retain the boundary/divisor barriers, periodic-domain and area conditions and the specified coherent orientation class. With the regular data and compactification/gluing construction supplied at that scope, apply F3 to the marked Seifert surface F. Its meridional frame, rather than an unspecified closure framing, gives an admissible adapted representative. By F4 every generator has Alexander degree g−n_P(x), with n_P(x) a nonnegative integer. Hence its whole integral chain complex has no generator, and thus no homology, in a grading greater than g. [F3, F4, F6, step 1.3]
